title: Film Kit
question: How does Film Kit rebuild a film's editions from its tracked sources, and what holds each step to its inputs?
summary: A pinned local voice model narrates each edition thought by thought; one soundtrack is assembled at one program level, the captions are timed, the picture is gated and rendered, and four films are packaged: a UHD master and a 1080p film, each with and without captions. Each step records the SHA-256 of what it read, and a later step refuses a record bound to other bytes.
scope: The Film Kit engine as released at v0.35.0: the src/filmkit package, with its Python modules, Node tools and watch list, and the pyproject.toml and VERSION that package it.
limits: A component lists only the files under the paths it claims, and a relation only the modules that make its call or run its process.

A relation shows only a call or process call in the source, not runtime order. Four kinds of call are not drawn, and the web page names them: most reads of Spoken units and of Film and editions; the calls Verification and Review make across the build; Take judgment's calls into Alignment and selection; and the runs of the narration command by Auditions and script edits.
Tests, the sample film, the OpenSpec specifications and changes, the documentation and the repository's tooling and CI are outside the scope.

exclude.reason: The engine's Python and Node tests.
The sample film that the tests load and the local acceptance builds; its text is written for the tests and is no film's source.
The engine's OpenSpec specifications and archived Changes: its accepted requirements and change history.
The README, the agent entry, the contributing guide and the change log; the guide cites them at the same revision.
The copyright notice and the licences of the sample film's assets and of the software and models a build installs.
The development lock; a film locks filmkit and its dependencies in its own project.
The npm packages that the tests and the sample film use; a film declares its own.
The lock of those npm packages.
Tool configuration: the Mise tasks and lock, linters, formatters and the CI projection.
The repository's ETHOS binding and release peers.
The proof sets that ETHOS and hosted CI run for this repository.

overview.claim: Each edition rebuilt from the film's own sources
overview.lead: A local engine: Film Kit narrates, assembles, captions, gates, renders and packages each edition of a narrated explainer film, and every step records the SHA-256 of what it read.

blocks.title: Before anything is narrated
items: Concepts
each segment says its declared concepts in approved words; no declared counterexample appears anywhere
Readings
each watched Chinese character has a declared reading, and every name a spoken form
Spoken text
one pronunciation contract per edition derives what each thought says
Refusal
filmkit check names every failure at once; narration is refused until it passes

blocks.title: Before the picture renders
items: Frame audit
at 30 frames per second: layout, legibility, balance and how text lines up
Sync audit
each label against its spoken words; any mark whose name is late
Text measures
the declared title shows for 1 s before the first word; text at rest has a contrast of 4.5:1 or more
Motion audit
ghosts, stalls, pops, jumps and dash snaps at 30 frames per second
Detail audit
single lines, strokes and names, through every frame at 60 frames per second
Gate record
picture-gates, with a verdict; the picture renders only after a pass

blocks.title: A take reaches the soundtrack only if it ends naturally
blocks.note: A natural ending is quiet: the last syllable dies away instead of stopping short.

stations.label: Seed
stations.note: the cast's seed, or a retake

stations.label: Select
stations.note: bound to the script and the cast

aside.label: Abrupt: audition other seeds, or read on into the next thought and cut in the quiet, then bind the chosen seed to the thought's text and speech. The assembly refuses an abrupt take unless the film declares a tail release for its join.

details.runs: one verb of a film's build in the film's folder: supply, check, edit, narrate, plan, build, verify, review, deliver or release
details.calls: the owner of what each verb does; plan and build through the build graph
details.refuses: in one line on standard error with status 1; a command that cannot finish exits 2
details.retires: each retired module command, run with python -m, in one line that names its verb

details.runs: synthesis, alignment and transcription, each as its own step
details.refuses: before any step while the plan calls the edition's narration not ready, as while the source check is stale or refused

details.finds: the film that FILMKIT_ROOT names, or the nearest content/film.toml
details.declares: file prefix, editions, fonts, player colours, review policy and source manifest, checked before any work
details.fixes: 60 fps, 48 kHz, -16.5 LUFS, and a UHD master and a 1080p film, each with and without captions
details.languages: one declaration for each language the engine builds; a film's editions are the languages it names

details.concepts: each segment says its declared concepts in approved words, and no counterexample appears
details.readings: each watched Chinese character has a declared reading, and each name a spoken form
details.terms: each declared Latin-script term is spelled alike for the narrator and said like the occurrence a person heard correct
details.register: the words a viewer meets outside the picture, against the formal register, with the Vale the engine pins
details.asks: every question of the film's sources at once with filmkit check, the film-wide node that every heavy or GPU node waits for

details.narrates: each thought natively with the pinned voice model, from the cast's seed or retake
details.divides: the segments a narration has to generate among processes of the voice model, one for every 16 GB of the host's memory, at most three
details.derives: each thought's spoken text through its edition's pronunciation contract
details.reuses: a take whose request fingerprint and recording still match

details.auditions: other seeds of a thought, and proposes a take that no line of the judgment refuses
details.converges: an edition's narration with no targets file, phrase or seed from its author: it runs the narration command for what is due, judges every thought, generates candidates for each refused one and binds the accepted candidate with the widest margin; then it counts the settled edition by the assembly's own count, which states its runtime
details.binds: the chosen seed to the thought's exact text and speech
details.edits: thoughts in place, moving each retake with its text

details.judges: a take of one thought by every line the film holds for a take: its length, ending, phrase ends, opening, unmarked pauses, declared terms, units and clarity, and names every failing line at once
details.holds: a take to its words: no unit of its transcript may differ from its text by reading
details.chooses: among the takes no line refuses, the one with the widest margin, then the quietest ending, then the lowest seed
details.asks: the selection's gates about each segment as they will measure it, where the narration's alignment stands beside the receipt; it transcribes each take with the pinned recognizer
details.writes: judgment.json beside an edition's narration receipt, with each thought's measures, its verdict on each line and the lines it fails
details.settles: only the lines that the author's hearing of one take names, for that take alone

details.aligns: each recording to its exact text with the pinned forced aligner
details.transcribes: each recording as a recognition proxy, not certification, and caches each transcript under its waveform, the language and the recognizer's identity
details.selects: the recordings and alignment bound to the current script and cast, within the film's pause limits and declared terms
details.hears: an English transcript's words by their pronunciation in the pinned CMUdict

details.installs: the pinned browser build, CMUdict and three speech models, each checked against its digests
details.network: the only step that reaches it

details.names: the spoken units, punctuation roles, joins and thought spans that sound, captions and audits share
details.measures: the heard pause at each word boundary, which selection and assembly limit, and the steps between thoughts, for listening
details.anchors: the anchors a segment marks in its own words, each placed by time in the timeline

details.assembles: the selected takes with designed pauses at one program level
details.refuses: a take that ends abruptly without a declared tail release, an unmarked pause above its limit, and a declared term said unlike its reference
details.writes: the soundtrack, the timeline, the assembly receipt and the sound gate's record
details.judges: the assembled soundtrack by the review's measures, and refuses a segment under the film's clarity floor, an abrupt or cut ending and a stopped phrase
details.levels: on the tolerances a script declares, each thought within its segment, each segment within its chapter and each chapter within the film, each by one static gain

details.times: one-line cues on the exact aligned words, never across a thought
details.typesets: each cue's text, with typographic quotation marks; the narration and aligned words stay as written
details.writes: SRT, VTT, the transcript, the chapters and their metadata

details.audits: every frame at 1/30 s, each label's sync with its words, the opening title and each text's contrast, motion at 30 fps, and single lines, strokes and names at 60 fps
details.keeps: a finding of the detail audit or a run far off centre that the film declares as an exception, recorded with its reason
details.binds: composition, timeline, stylesheet, fonts and engine version in the gate record
details.refuses: each anchor the picture reads that the edition does not mark

details.runs: the engine's Node tools with the film's npm packages, from a copy in the film's tool cache
details.measures: text by the advance widths of the film's declared faces
details.ends: a tool that cannot finish with status 2, which no refusal may stand on

details.runs: the film's composition headlessly on a canvas stand-in
details.measures: layout, legibility, balance, typography, the label and text traces, motion, and the detail of single lines, strokes and names
details.compares: each uncaptioned frame's paints with the captioned frame's, less its caption paints
details.proves: that the rows a derived uncaptioned picture paints hold caption paints and nothing else
details.weighs: the mass of each scene's lit paints on the uncaptioned stage, drawn as the renderer draws it

details.checks: the staged picture's geometry and the delivered players in Chrome Headless Shell
details.paints: each edition's cover from the staged picture
details.draws: each whole turn the frame audit found, to find the arcs the browser paints without ink
details.names: the browser its checks run: the build the supply installs, or the one FILM_CHROMIUM_PATH names
details.takes: the picture's size, seconds and rate from the stage's record, and refuses a stage whose page states another size or length

details.stages: the picture's data, the composition's script and style, the fonts and one document that inlines them, bound in stage.json with the faces and the language
details.reads: every @font-face rule of the film's stylesheet once, for the audits' text table and the renderer, and refuses by name a rule it cannot hold the canvas to
details.renders: the captioned picture, and the uncaptioned one where it is not derived, with the native renderer only after a passing gate record
details.derives: the uncaptioned picture from the captioned one, for a film that declares software capture and a captioned picture the pinned canvas build drew, by one x264 encode that paints the caption band's rows in the ground
details.validates: each rendered picture's receipt, which must name the engine's canvas package, version and text renderer, its frames, size and cadence, and a keyframe every 2 s; a derived picture against its derivation's receipt
details.qualifies: the renderer by a second render of the captioned stage in another count of spans: the two must state one digest of their drawn frames and compare with no row left out
details.scans: a draft, and each edition's packaged 1080p captioned film, for speech over a still picture; the film's scan decides
details.compares: each edition's two pictures before packaging: a rendered pair at every frame, which may differ only by its captions and must keep its edge slivers within the bound; a derived pair by the derivation's receipt, decoding no picture

details.draws: a staged picture by running the film's composition on a canvas of @napi-rs/canvas with the host's text renderer, and no browser
details.encodes: each frame through x264 with a keyframe every 2 s and no B-frames; a picture in four spans of whole groups of frames, one process each, joined by stream copy, and a draft in one process
details.pins: @napi-rs/canvas 1.1.1 and, for Apple silicon, the SHA-256 of its native library; a film that installs another version is refused
details.records: in each render receipt the canvas package with its version and integrity, the native library the render loaded, the text renderer, the operating system, the spans, the frames and a digest of every drawn frame

details.packages: four films (a UHD master and a 1080p film, each with and without captions), with cover, release tags and chapters; each 1080p film encoded by x264 in software and keyed every 2 s, and no film with B-frames
details.derives: the viewing package: cover, subtitles, transcript, chapters and the player, which the engine renders
details.sets: the chapter track's language in place
details.names: the film's version from its VERSION, in each film and on both pages
details.holds: the entry page to its rule: one link to each edition's player, in the declared order

details.verifies: sources, narration custody, both pictures and their equivalence, both packages, the still scan of the 1080p captioned film, every decoded film and the review
details.reads back: the keywords and authors Spotlight imports from each film, where the host has mdimport
details.refuses: a caption cue whose text is not typeset

details.compares: a rebuild with the published release: bytes, decoded audio, container, and each frame's PSNR
details.writes: the release manifest from the reviewed, delivered build, and stages the assets it names

details.delivers: the 25 delivery members to the film's delivery folder, then reads them back
details.destination: the folder filmkit deliver --to names, else the film's declared delivery_folder below the root FILMKIT_DELIVERY_ROOT names, else that name below the user's videos folder
details.refuses: a destination it must not fill, such as the film's root, or an edition without its passing still scan, before anything is read back or changed
details.reads: the entry page and both players back in a real browser before rsync changes anything

details.prepares: an independent review round: set-aside, a preparation by one command with the player binding and prompts, and records
details.measures: rate, pauses, endings, levels, voice clarity, recognition and the picture records
details.reads: a segment's voice clarity over the whole soundtrack's kept frames whose centres lie in it, as the reviewers do
details.judges: each thought's ending by the criterion the assembly uses

details.reads: streams, frame cadence, complete decodes and loudness through FFprobe and FFmpeg

details.ends: the children a command started when the command is asked to end, so that none outlives it
details.takes: an interrupt, SIGTERM or a hang-up only while the command holds a renderer, a narration's processes or a step of narrate
details.waits: for a child it asked to end as many seconds as its caller names, by default twice as long as the child may wait for its own children
details.exits: with one line that names the request, and the status a shell expects

details.records: a run record of every run of a node: each input and output by path, size, time and SHA-256, the engine and its pins, the outcome, and the run's start, seconds, phases and the host's 1-minute load at both ends
details.plans: each node's state (fresh, stale, behind or waiting), its host class and whether it is ready, from the run records, with filmkit plan
details.builds: the targets fresh, one node at a time in the derived order, with filmkit build
details.verifies: every recorded file by its SHA-256, and refuses bytes that no record of a declared writer accounts for, with filmkit verify

details.packages: src/filmkit as one wheel, its Node tools included
details.depends: mlx-audio 0.6.6, NumPy, Pillow, Pydantic, pypinyin and snowballstemmer
details.records: the npm packages it runs in a film, the versions of the Python packages its dependencies resolve to and the version of Vale, in released.json
details.offers: filmkit.api and the Node test entry picture/testing.mjs, the only names a film's own tests import

details.holds: the declaration, scripts, casts, pronunciation contract, pages, review policy and picture composition

details.browser: Chrome Headless Shell 152.0.7977.30, for the geometry check, the whole-turn gate, the cover and the players' checks

details.tools: FFmpeg with libx264, ExifTool and rsync 3, from Homebrew; Vale, at the version the engine's record states, through Mise

details.scores: each edition on the film's declared dimensions

views.title: From a film's sources to its packaged films
views.question: Which commands carry one edition from its script to its four packaged films?
views.summary: The narration command hands synthesis to Thought takes. Through the build graph, the console command assembles the soundtrack, refreshes captions, checks the picture, renders it only after a passing gate record and packages four films. Every node's run writes a run record.

views.title: What the engine reads from a film
views.question: Which component reads the film's declaration, and what must hold before narration?
views.summary: The part Film and editions reads the film repository's declaration and checks it before any work. filmkit check runs Word checks on concepts, register, readings and terms at once; while that check is stale or refused, narration is refused before any speech model loads.

views.title: Narration and its supply
views.question: How is each thought narrated, auditioned and aligned, and what does Supply install first?
views.summary: Thought takes reads each thought aloud from the cast's seed or retake, and Auditions and script edits tries other seeds; Take judgment judges each take by every line the film holds for it; Alignment and selection aligns each recording to its text; Supply installs the browser build, the pinned CMUdict and three speech models. A narration run that is asked to end leaves no process behind.

views.title: One assembly for sound and captions
views.question: How do the selected takes become one soundtrack, a timeline and its captions?
views.summary: Soundtrack assembly lays out the selected takes with designed pauses, brings the whole to one program level, writes the soundtrack and timeline, and refuses abrupt takes. Each cue is timed by Captions on the aligned words; no cue spans two thoughts.

views.title: The picture's gate and render
views.question: What audits the picture before it renders, and what renders it?
views.summary: The picture gate has the Node tool runner run the frame, motion, detail and mass audits and binds the composition, fonts and engine version in its gate record. Picture rendering has the native renderer draw each stage only after a passing record, on a canvas and with no browser.

views.title: Packaging, verification, delivery and review
views.question: What checks the four packaged films, and what is a rebuild compared with?
views.summary: Packaging encodes four films; Verification reads each record and decodes each film; Delivery sends the delivery folder its 25 members and reads them back. Review writes prompts for the independent reviewer; Reproduction compares a rebuild with the published release.
